root_cause.text: In `drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-svs.c`, `svs_enable_debug_write()` allocates user input with `memdup_user_nul()` but on the `kstrtoint()` error path it returns without freeing `buf`, causing a memory leak in the SVS debugfs write handler.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly says “the buf allocated by memdup_user_nul() is leaked if kstrtoint() fails,” and the patch fixes this by changing `char *buf = NULL;` to `char *buf __free(kfree) = NULL;` and removing the explicit `kfree(buf);`, showing the leak was due to missing cleanup on failure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the cleanup header so the file can use kernel cleanup helpers.
intent_record.what: A new include directive for <linux/cleanup.h> was added alongside the existing kernel header includes.
intent_record.how: This makes cleanup-related kernel helpers/macros available to the file at compile time, enabling use of automatic resource cleanup patterns in subsequent code.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add automatic kfree cleanup for the debug write buffer to prevent memory leaks.
intent_record.what: In svs_enable_debug_write(), the local pointer declaration for buf changed from `char *buf = NULL;` to `char *buf __free(kfree) = NULL;`, adding an automatic cleanup attribute that will call kfree on scope exit.
intent_record.how: This changes runtime resource handling so that any memory later assigned to buf will be freed automatically when the function returns, reducing the risk of leaks on success or error paths without changing the function’s visible control flow.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the incorrect kfree() from svs_enable_debug_write() to fix buffer lifetime handling.
intent_record.what: The call to kfree(buf); was removed from the end of svs_enable_debug_write() before returning count.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer frees the buffer at this point, which changes ownership/lifetime handling for buf and avoids a potential premature or duplicate free if the buffer is managed elsewhere.

relevance_review.reason: The change only adds a cleanup header to enable kernel cleanup helpers, but it does not directly modify the vulnerable debugfs write path or fix the missing free of the memdup_user_nul() buffer on the kstrtoint() error path.
The change directly addresses the reported memory leak in the SVS debugfs write handler by adding automatic kfree cleanup for the allocated user buffer, which matches the root cause.

The change directly concerns svs_enable_debug_write() buffer handling, which is the exact area of the reported memory leak. Even though the summary says it removes an incorrect kfree(), it is part of fixing the user-input buffer lifetime in the same function and is related to the vulnerability root cause.

candidates.rationale: This buffer is allocated later from user input and, in the buggy pre-fix flow, it could be left unfreed on the kstrtoint() error path, causing the leak described in the root cause.
In the vulnerable version, the error path returned from the write handler without ensuring buf was freed, so the return path itself embodies the leak-prone control flow.

vuln_statements.explanation: This parse step is the one whose failure path triggers the leak: when kstrtoint() returns an error after buf was allocated by memdup_user_nul(), the pre-fix control flow returned without freeing buf.
